breakdown.description: Thin airfoil theory (linear small-angle model) is applied at a large angle of attack where stall/nonlinear effects dominate.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification repeats and even reinforces the original error. It applies thin airfoil theory at 20 degrees angle of attack and explicitly states 'Do not account for stall or nonlinear effects; treat the relationship as fully linear.' The ground truth requires either reducing the angle of attack to a small value (e.g., 5 degrees) or using a nonlinear/stall model or experimental data for 20 degrees. The agent failed to identify or correct this inconsistency.
